name: Atticus
cost: Free and open source (MIT). It uses your paid Claude Pro or Max plan, about 0.18¢ of plan usage per ask
works_with: macOS 26 or later, through Claude Code. A separate Windows version exists
short: Hold a shortcut, say what you need, and it moves windows, finds files, reads your screen or plays music on your Mac.
what: Atticus is a hold-to-talk voice assistant for macOS. Hold Control, Option and Space, speak, and let go. Simple asks like opening an app or moving a window run without any AI. Everything else goes through `claude -p` on the Claude plan you already pay for. It also remembers rules you give it, can watch a window or page for you, and has an optional Meeting Copilot that keeps transcripts.
who: Mac users on macOS 26 who already pay for Claude Pro or Max and want to drive their computer by voice. Skip it if you're on an older macOS, don't have a paid Claude plan, or don't want an assistant with Accessibility and screen access.
needs: macOS 26 or later (it uses Apple's on-device speech)
A paid Claude plan (Pro or Max) and Claude Code. The setup window can install Claude Code and sign you in
Accessibility permission, for clicks, scrolling, menus and typing inside apps

steps.title: Run the installer in Terminal
steps.text: It checks your Mac, downloads Atticus to `~/.atticus`, builds `~/Applications/Atticus.app` and opens it.

steps.title: Finish setup
steps.text: The first launch checks your Claude plan and asks for each macOS permission. After that Atticus lives in the menu bar. Open it from Spotlight to change the shortcut, model, memory and other settings.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Anywhere on your Mac, holding Control + Option + Space
try.text: "Code on my big screen, Chrome and Terminal on the laptop." Then try "When I say focus mode, close Slack and open my to-do list."

watch: The README tells you to pipe a download straight into bash. Read `install.sh` first.
It starts at login and updates itself. You can turn updates off in Settings, About & Updates.

It gets Accessibility access and can read your screen. Safe mode runs the AI's commands in Claude Code's sandbox, asks before anything deletes, sends, buys or changes a file, and always blocks `rm`, `sudo`, disk tools and shutdown.
Once a day it sends a random ID to PostHog to count users. Turn it off under Settings, Account & Access, Count me as a user.
Help improve Atticus is off until you agree. If on, failed tasks send what you asked and the steps taken, with emails, numbers and paths removed first.
Meeting Copilot saves transcripts by default under `~/.config/atticus/meetings/`. AI summaries send the transcript to Claude on your plan. Audio is never saved.
Voice is turned into text on your Mac by Apple's speech. Audio never leaves your Mac.
